name: Fakeverse
description: Coherent fake data generator themed by fictional universes: Python package, Faker provider, CLI and HTTP API.
description_good_justification: https://github.com/Kentrow/fakeverse/blob/main/README.md - the first paragraph of the README says what the software does.
interact_justification: https://github.com/Kentrow/fakeverse/blob/main/README.md explains how to install and use it; https://github.com/Kentrow/fakeverse/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md how to report problems and contribute.
contribution_requirements_justification: https://github.com/Kentrow/fakeverse/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md - content rules for universe files, code rules, tests, Conventional Commits and DCO sign-off.
floss_license_justification: Code under MIT, universe data files under CC0-1.0.
floss_license_osi_justification: The code is under MIT, an OSI-approved license. The universe data files are dedicated to the public domain with CC0-1.0.
documentation_interface_justification: Python API, Faker provider and CLI in https://github.com/Kentrow/fakeverse/blob/main/README.md and https://github.com/Kentrow/fakeverse/blob/main/docs/generation.md; HTTP API in https://github.com/Kentrow/fakeverse/blob/main/docs/api.md and https://github.com/Kentrow/fakeverse/blob/main/docs/problems.md, plus the OpenAPI document served at /docs.
sites_https_justification: The repository, the issue tracker and the package (PyPI) and image (GHCR) registries are only served over HTTPS.
discussion_justification: GitHub issues (https://github.com/Kentrow/fakeverse/issues) and Discussions (https://github.com/Kentrow/fakeverse/discussions): searchable, addressable by URL, open to new participants, no proprietary client needed.
english_justification: Documentation, code, issues and pull requests are in English.
maintained_justification: Actively maintained: issues, pull requests and dependency updates are handled continuously, see the commit history.
repo_interim_justification: Every change goes through a public pull request, merged into main between releases.
version_unique_justification: Each release has a unique version, published once on PyPI and as a v* git tag.
version_tags_justification: Each release is tagged vX.Y.Z (https://github.com/Kentrow/fakeverse/tags); a ruleset protects v* tags.
release_notes_justification: https://github.com/Kentrow/fakeverse/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md (Keep a Changelog) and the GitHub releases (https://github.com/Kentrow/fakeverse/releases).
release_notes_vulns_justification: The changelog has a Security section for vulnerability fixes. No publicly known vulnerability has been fixed in a release so far.
report_process_justification: https://github.com/Kentrow/fakeverse/issues, with issue forms for bugs, data fixes, features and new universes.
report_responses_justification: No bug report has come from outside the project yet; the maintainer answers every report in the issue tracker.
enhancement_responses_justification: No enhancement request has come from outside the project yet; the maintainer answers them in the issues or the Discussions.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Private vulnerability reporting with GitHub security advisories: https://github.com/Kentrow/fakeverse/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability has been reported in the last 6 months. SECURITY.md commits to an acknowledgment within 72 hours.
build_justification: Standard Python build with hatchling: uv build produces the wheel and the sdist; the Dockerfile builds the API image.
build_floss_tools_justification: uv, hatchling, Docker and every build dependency are open source.
test_justification: pytest suite in https://github.com/Kentrow/fakeverse/tree/main/tests (unit, API, property-based and golden tests), run with uv run pytest.
test_most_justification: The suite covers 99% of the lines and branches; CI fails below 90%.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions run the full suite on Python 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14 on every pull request and push: https://github.com/Kentrow/fakeverse/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
test_policy_justification: https://github.com/Kentrow/fakeverse/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md: every feature comes with its tests and the CI must stay green; the pull request template checks it.
tests_are_added_justification: Recent changes come with their tests, see the merged pull requests: https://github.com/Kentrow/fakeverse/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged
warnings_justification: ruff (pycodestyle, pyflakes, bugbear, pylint and more) and mypy --strict run in pre-commit and CI.
warnings_fixed_justification: CI fails on any ruff or mypy warning; main has none.
warnings_strict_justification: mypy runs in --strict mode and ruff enables a broad rule set.
crypto_published_justification: Fakeverse implements no security mechanism based on cryptography. blake2b only derives deterministic generation seeds and ETags, not a security function.
crypto_call_justification: Fakeverse does not implement cryptographic functions; TLS is left to the reverse proxy in front of the API.
crypto_floss_justification: No cryptography is used for security.
crypto_working_justification: No cryptography is used for security.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No cryptography is used for security.
crypto_pfs_justification: The API does not terminate TLS; that is the job of the reverse proxy (see docs/deployment.md).
crypto_password_storage_justification: Fakeverse stores no passwords: there is no authentication.
crypto_random_justification: No cryptographic keys or nonces are generated. Seeds drawn when none is given come from secrets.randbits, but they are not secrets.
delivery_mitm_justification: Releases are delivered over HTTPS by PyPI and GHCR, with signed build provenance for the distributions (PEP 740 attestations on PyPI, GitHub artifact attestations).
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hash is retrieved over HTTP. Locked dependencies are installed with their hashes from uv.lock.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No known vulnerability is left unpatched: Dependabot security updates are merged as soon as they are opened, and pip-audit runs in CI.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: Critical vulnerabilities are fixed as soon as they are reported.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credentials in the repository: gitleaks runs in pre-commit, GitHub secret scanning with push protection is enabled, and publishing uses trusted publishing (OIDC) without stored tokens.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL (Python and GitHub Actions) on every pull request, push and weekly; ruff, mypy --strict and zizmor (workflow security) in pre-commit and CI: https://github.com/Kentrow/fakeverse/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL security queries look for common vulnerabilities (injection, open redirect...); zizmor looks for insecure GitHub Actions workflows.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Findings are fixed before merging; a CodeQL open redirect finding was fixed in #2 before the first release.
static_analysis_often_justification: On every pull request and every push to main.
dynamic_analysis_justification: Property-based and fuzz tests with Hypothesis: universe validation never crashes and accepted universes generate coherent data (tests/property), and the HTTP API never answers 500 whatever the request (tests/api/test_api_fuzz.py). They run in CI on every pull request.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: Fakeverse is written in Python, a memory-safe language.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Tests run with Python assertions enabled, and Hypothesis checks invariants on generated inputs.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: Defects found by the fuzz tests are fixed before release; none is outstanding.
